messages.subject: Question on Code for Section 6.1.2
parts:
Dear INLA community,

I have a question on the code for Section 6.1.2.

The original code is as follows:

# The order of the areas needs to be the same between the data and the spatial polygon object obtained importing the shapefile, so we re-order the data
data.boroughs <- attr(london.gen, "data")
order <- match(data.boroughs$NAME,data.suicides$NAME)
data.suicides <- data.suicides[order,]
data.suicides$ID <- seq(1,Nareas)
# Include in the london.gen dataframe the ID variable  1:32 (because SP_Id is 0:31)
attr(london.gen, "data") <- merge(data.boroughs,data.suicides,by="NAME")

mod.suicides <- inla(formula,family="poisson",
              data=data.suicides,E=E,
              control.compute=list(dic=TRUE))

When I run the code data.boroughs <- attr(london.gen, "data"), the data.boroughs variable does not contain any values.


I tried a different approach to order the data.suicides dataframe, but I encountered another issue after running the subsequent code.
# The order of the areas needs to be the same between the data and the spatial polygon object obtained importing the shapefile, so we re-order the data

rownames(london.gen) <- london.gen$NAME
rownames(data.suicides) <- data.suicides$NAME
data.suicides <- data.suicides[match(rownames(london.gen), rownames(data.suicides)),]
rownames(london.gen) <- NULL
rownames(data.suicides) <- NULL

> mod.suicides <- inla(formula,family="poisson", + data=data.suicides,E=E, + control.compute=list(dic=TRUE)) *** inla.core.safe: The inla program failed, but will rerun in case better initial values may help. try=1/1 Error in inla.core.safe(formula = formula, family = family, contrasts = contrasts, : NData > 0 is not TRUE The inla program failed and the maximum number of tries has been reached.

I would appreciate it if you could help me resolve this problem.

Thank you very much

Best wishes,
Mingming

Hi,
as there are several books, please specify which book you are referring to. (You might also have better luck resolving the problem by contacting the author of that specific book)  From the error message it seems something has changed in the format or code for the data that the example uses, so that it's no longer stored in the way assumed by the code.

Finn
